source.title: Parcae: Scaling Laws For Stable Looped Language Models
source.authors: Hayden Prairie; Zachary Novack; Taylor Berg-Kirkpatrick; Daniel Y. Fu

record.tranche_reason: The study measures scaling laws in looped language models, a new architecture and scaling axis; it does not reproduce the original fixed-depth parameter/data scaling experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper reports loss fits using effective unrolled parameters and tokens, held-out loss predictions, and compute-optimal recurrence/data allocations. Its downstream score comparisons are recorded where they bear on downstream scaling. Comparisons of Parcae with RDMs and Transformers that do not measure scaling-law behavior, and cited results from other work, are not recorded as claim rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests a pretraining loss power law in a new looped-language-model setting. Its token and effective-parameter loss fits bear on V1, but recurrence allocation, held-out prediction without large-scale extrapolation, and matched-budget architecture comparisons do not establish the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record largely captures the authors' scaling conclusion, but 'under fixed compute' needs clarification: across increasing compute budgets, optimal recurrence and tokens increase together while actual parameter count stays fixed. The authors also conclude that inference recurrence follows a saturating exponential and acknowledge that the scaling-law experiments use small architectures. Their claim that the loss-optimal frontier consistently translates into higher downstream scores is contradicted by several entries in Tables 6 and 16.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Hoffmann-style isoFLOP, parabolic, and parametric loss fits, but applies them to effective unrolled parameters and recurrence in looped Parcae models rather than ordinary parameter-count scaling.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that the compute-optimal allocation is estimated by parabolic fits; training and test-time results also depend on recurrence and backpropagation depth. Its unified test-time fit reports a modest benefit from learning the recurrence conditioning exponent rather than fixing it to 1.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed actual parameter count, fitted optimal recurrence grows approximately as compute^0.38–0.40 and optimal tokens as compute^0.77–0.78.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compute-optimal recurrence and tokens follow power laws in the tested Parcae setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Training-law predictions for held-out 140M and 370M configurations have reported validation-loss errors of 1.3% and 0.8%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The fitted recurrence/token training law generalizes to held-out configurations at the tested base model sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: Loss-optimal looping has mixed downstream results against fixed depth at equal compute, including clear deficits at the largest reported budgets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizing recurrence for validation loss does not consistently improve downstream scores over allocating the same compute to more tokens.

fits_no_version.finding: Inference recurrence loss is better fitted by a saturating exponential than the tested power-law alternatives; the unified law predicts held-out curves within 0.85–1.31% average error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parcae inference recurrence follows a saturating exponential whose floor and decay depend on training.

record.problems: The training scaling-law sweep covers only 140M and 370M base models and is described by the authors as limited to small architectures. The fitted loss law and held-out predictions are evaluated in a narrow setup, and held-out prediction is not tested across orders of magnitude. Downstream score comparisons show mixed outcomes across compute budgets.
record.rows_left_out: End-to-end benchmark and perplexity comparisons in Tables 3–5 were omitted because they compare architectures rather than report a fitted scaling-law prediction. Other test-time fit diagnostics and appendix ablations were not included beyond the test-time fit results and held-out unified prediction reported in r45–r49.

untested.parts: Ordinary independent parameter-count scaling, non-bottleneck one-axis sweeps, and persistence over several orders of magnitude. The fitted parameter axis represents unrolled recurrence.
Prediction from small runs to training runs orders of magnitude larger; held-out configurations at the same two base sizes do not establish this.
Joint optimal actual parameter-count and token-count scaling with compute. Actual parameter count is fixed within each recurrence/token sweep.
Loss insensitivity across a wide range of depth, width, and architecture choices under a controlled shape comparison.
Power-law scaling in other modalities or other training regimes. Inference recurrence curves measure a different axis.
A predictive relationship connecting downstream scores to training scale or pretraining loss. The recorded downstream rows compare recurrence allocations at matched compute.

Sensitivity of pretraining power-law exponents and actual parameter/token optima to fitting choices or setup, and disagreement between published laws. Inference functional-form diagnostics do not establish this version.

record.verdict_notes: All recorded numerical values match the supplied text. Removing version links does not invalidate those measurements; it removes interpretations they cannot establish. Limited experimental coverage belongs under untested, not a limits_scope verdict. The downstream states in the record describe advantage over a competing allocation, which differs from V6's improvement with scale or loss.

versions.untested_parts: Does not independently sweep ordinary model parameter count, tokens, and training compute over several orders of magnitude; its fitted parameter quantity is effective parameterization N(µrec) for looped models.
Tests predictions on held-out models/settings, but not runs orders of magnitude larger than the fitted runs.
The paper optimizes recurrence and tokens at fixed parameter count; it does not test the parameter-count/token allocation or the Kaplan-versus-Hoffmann parameter scaling trend.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
No other modalities, repeated-data regimes, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling-law tests.

Reports downstream scores across compute budgets and a comparison with fixed-depth models, but does not fit or validate a predictive law for downstream performance as a function of scale or pretraining loss.
Does not compare published exponents or compute-optimal parameter/token splits across fitting choices or setups.

relation.reason: Reports original isoFLOP experiments and fits additive power-law terms to held-out validation loss.

tranche.reason: Tests validation-loss scaling in a new setting: stable looped language models with variable recurrence and training tokens.

source_check.notes: Table 11's Huber values are fit diagnostics, not coefficient uncertainty. Effective parameters vary through recurrence at fixed actual model size; the authors acknowledge that their scaling experiments use small architectures.

reader_labels.label: supports

reader_labels.reason: The fitted loss function uses power-law terms for effective parameters and tokens, and the paper reports similar optimal-recurrence and token exponents across the two sizes (r1–r6).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The parameter term is effective parameterization induced by recurrence, and the scaling experiments cover only two base model sizes and limited FLOP budgets (r1–r6).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Downstream Core scores at 140M and 370M, at budgets where optimal looping beats fixed depth
reader_labels.reason: Optimal-looping models have higher Core scores at several compute budgets, including 2 and 8 × 10^18 for 140M and 32 × 10^18 for 370M (r14, r22, r34).
